definition: A system architecture where a cheap, fast model attempts a task first, escalating to a more powerful (and expensive) model only when needed, such as when confidence is low.
details: Model cascades aim to reduce average inference cost by reserving expensive model calls for genuinely difficult cases, while still handling most requests with a lightweight first-pass model.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Boil it down and it is this: A system architecture where a cheap, fast model attempts a task first, escalating to a more powerful (and expensive) model only when needed, such as when confidence is low. Here is why it matters: Model cascades aim to reduce average inference cost by reserving expensive model calls for genuinely difficult cases, while still handling most requests with a lightweight first-pass model. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Cascade (Model Cascade).
